analysis.title: Multi-Asset Strategy Daily
key_insights: Cash USTs were closed for Veterans Day while futures traded with a flattening bias as the front end sold off. After the reopening, 2Y yields are above 4.75% and the 10Y UST yield is just below 5.00%. Mizuho sees 10Y yields around 5% as fair value.
The DXY index continued to rise and is above 103. Risk sentiment is less supportive this morning, with S&P futures consolidating off yesterday's highs.

December is fully priced at 28bp of Fed hikes. Today's Fed speakers (Hammack, Goolsbee, Daly, Schmid, Williams) matter, particularly any willingness to entertain a jumbo hike. Jobless claims are the only meaningful data today, ahead of PPI tomorrow, which Mizuho expects to be the bigger test for the front end.

Mizuho argues against fading the front-end sell-off too aggressively, citing ongoing geopolitical risk premium and equities holding up. It expects the next macro catalyst to come from Fed communication today and PPI tomorrow.

Oil remains relevant for rates. VP Vance is reportedly considering direct talks with a senior Iranian security official as the administration looks for an off-ramp from the conflict. Mizuho sees little evidence of decisive de-escalation, and Brent has rebounded above $93pb.

EUR rates were quiet with US cash markets closed, but the curve bear-flattened into 10s as the front end extended Tuesday's selloff. The 10Y Bund traded around 3.30-3.35%, and a weak German 30Y auction yesterday left pressure further out the curve. Mizuho expects the front end to stay sensitive to US repricing and energy.
Italy supplies up to €7.25bn across 3Y, 7Y and 20Y Green BTPs this morning, putting peripheral demand in focus after BTPs outperformed yesterday.
ECB succession: France reportedly signalled it could back Hernandez de Cos to succeed Lagarde, and EU leaders may reach a deal as soon as this month.
EUR/USD fell below 1.11 and is near 1.1075, with the widening USD rate advantage dominating.

UK Q3 GDP came in line at 0.7% QoQ, the fastest pace since Q1-22, driven by household consumption, gross fixed capital formation and government spending. Mizuho sees the UK economy as more resilient than expected despite higher energy prices and cost-of-living pressure.

BoE's Greene struck a hawkish tone late Wednesday, arguing for proactive tightening to head off wage-driven inflation and questioning how much labour market slack exists. Mizuho says this keeps a December BoE move alive and the front end sticky around current pricing. 2Y Gilts cheapened about 5bp yesterday toward 4.93%, near the recent 4.96% high, and 10s pushed toward 5.25%. A £4bn 2033 auction is today's test. GBP/USD is under pressure near 1.3265, though the domestic picture should support GBP versus EUR.

Asian risk sentiment soured following NVDA's leadership crisis. JGBs recovered on dovish comments from BoJ's Asada, with the ultra-long end outperforming amid strong PPI data. USD/JPY continues to grind toward 160 and is finding some resistance there.

macro_indicators.interpretation: In line with expectations and the fastest pace since Q1-22. Supports the view that the UK economy is resilient, keeping a December BoE move alive and the front end sticky.
Market pricing is already aggressive, so Fed speakers' willingness to validate a jumbo hike is the key test.
Mizuho sees about 5% as fair value for 10Y yields.
The front-end sell-off drives a flattening bias in the curve.
Geopolitical risk premium persists, which argues against fading the front-end sell-off aggressively.

risk_factors: Fed officials could validate an increasingly aggressive hiking path, including a jumbo hike, pushing front-end yields higher.
Hot PPI tomorrow could extend the front-end sell-off.
Ongoing Iran conflict with limited de-escalation keeps oil and the rates risk premium elevated.
Weak demand at long-end auctions (German 30Y yesterday, £4bn 2033 Gilt today) adds pressure further out the curve.
NVDA's leadership crisis is souring risk sentiment.
vol_and_positioning: The December Fed hike is fully priced at 28bp. Mizuho cautions against fading the front-end sell-off too aggressively given the geopolitical risk premium and resilient equities.
geopolitical: VP Vance is reportedly considering direct talks with a senior Iranian security official as the administration looks for an off-ramp from the conflict. Little evidence of decisive de-escalation so far.
ECB succession race: France reportedly signalling support for Hernandez de Cos to succeed Lagarde, with EU leaders looking for a deal potentially this month.
